assessment.nobel_worthiness: Theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall state and Z2 topological insulators, followed by its experimental realization in HgTe quantum wells, opened a whole class of materials defined by topology and protected edge or surface states. The idea is original, conceptually clear and has changed how materials are classified and searched for. The 2016 prize recognized topological phase transitions and phases in general, but not this specific, concrete discovery.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical proposal and the Z2 classification; Molenkamp led the group that demonstrated quantum spin Hall edge transport experimentally. This gives a clean theory-plus-experiment trio. M. Zahid Hasan (ARPES observation of three-dimensional topological insulators) and the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang HgTe proposal do not fit within three places, so some allocation of credit remains unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Experiments are well reproduced and independent across many materials over nearly two decades; the interpretation is stable. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: How to treat Hasan's three-dimensional topological insulator observations and the HgTe theory proposal when only three places exist.
Whether the committee regards the 2016 prize as already covering the topic.
I rely on my own knowledge of the priority history and have not independently verified it.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on the magic-wavelength idea, reaches fractional uncertainty in the 10^-18 range and underpins the prospect of redefining the second, tests of fundamental physics and relativistic geodesy. It is a clear invention with large and lasting impact on precision measurement.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice clock concept and made the first demonstration; Ye led the push to the highest accuracy and stability and to many-body and clock-comparison applications. Others (for example Lemonde, Takamoto) contributed, but a two-person prize is well supported.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent laboratories confirm the performance; the field is mature. Redefinition of the second is still pending, though the physics is established. Timing is good.
uncertainties: Whether the committee will want a third contributor such as Pierre Lemonde.
The 2005 prize for frequency combs may create a perception of overlap in scope.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle and the experimental discovery of correlated insulator and superconducting states in twisted bilayer graphene created the field of moire quantum materials. It is original, has large and growing impact, and the experiment is conceptually crisp.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the quantitative continuum-model prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive experiments. This is a natural theory-plus-experiment configuration. Other experimental groups and earlier theory on twisted bilayers are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced widely since 2018 and still maturing; the origin of the superconductivity and broader correlated physics remain debated. Recognition may be a few years early.
uncertainties: Interpretation of the superconducting mechanism remains open.
Whether earlier theoretical work on twisted bilayers needs recognition.
Short time since the discovery relative to usual maturity expectations.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Correcting spherical aberration in electron lenses, long thought impossible, has brought atomic-resolution imaging and spectroscopy to sub-angstrom resolution and low accelerating voltages. The impact on materials physics is very large and lasting, and it is a clear invention. I flag my professional closeness to electron microscopy as a potential bias for the committee's conflict check.
assessment.attribution: Rose provided the theoretical design of the corrector, Haider built the first working corrector, and Urban demonstrated its power on materials. Krivanek and colleagues developed the competing scanning-microscope corrector and are not in the supplied credit, which leaves a real allocation issue.
assessment.maturity: Demonstrated in the late 1990s, commercially distributed for two decades and fully mature; recognition is timely or overdue.
uncertainties: Missing credit for the Krivanek/Dellby scanning corrector line.
Whether the prize would be seen as physics rather than instrumentation.
My professional proximity to electron microscopy may bias my judgement.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution is a fundamental use of quantum mechanics for information security, and entanglement-based protocols connect directly to Bell tests recognized in 2022. Originality and conceptual clarity are high; practical impact is real though deployment is limited.
assessment.attribution: BB84 by Bennett and Brassard and the entanglement-based protocol of Ekert are the central contributions; Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea is not in the list. The trio is natural, with a priority question about Wiesner and the relative weight of Ekert's protocol.
assessment.maturity: The theory is mature and implemented in field experiments and satellites; security proofs are well developed. Timeliness is good, especially after the 2022 prize.
uncertainties: Wiesner's priority is unresolved.
Real-device security loopholes may reduce perceived maturity.
Whether the committee views this as physics rather than computer science.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics gives strong coupling of superconducting qubits to microwave resonators, enabling dispersive readout and the architecture of many quantum processors. Importance is high and the discovery is clear.
assessment.attribution: Blais and colleagues made the theory proposal; Wallraff and Schoelkopf made the first experimental demonstrations in 2004. This gives a sensible theory plus two-experimentalists configuration.
assessment.maturity: Widely reproduced and a basis for large technology programs. Because the 2025 prize recognized macroscopic quantum effects in superconducting circuits, timing for a further award on this topic may be early.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2025 recognition of superconducting circuit work and its effect on timing.
Whether others with qubit-related contributions should be included.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realize Hubbard models and the superfluid to Mott insulator transition, creating quantum simulators for many-body physics. The influence is lasting and the experimental trajectory is clear.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller proposed the relevant theory; Bloch, Greiner and Esslinger carried out the decisive experiments. Five names are supplied, so a choice must be made between theory and experiment. I choose the experimental trio, but a theory-led split is a serious alternative.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely reproduced, though low-temperature fermionic Hubbard simulation is still progressing.
uncertainties: Allocation between theory (Zoller, Cirac) and experiment.
Relative priority of Greiner and Bloch's group.
Temperatures where d-wave physics appears have not been reached.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Observation of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos with IceCube opened neutrino astronomy and was followed by evidence for the blazar TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane. Importance and originality are high.
assessment.attribution: Halzen was the leading scientific driver of IceCube; Spiering and Karle had central roles, but the collaboration-wide effort makes attribution difficult and the committee must decide who is responsible for the original idea and its realization.
assessment.maturity: The 2013 detection is confirmed by multiple analyses, but source identification is still developing and the origin of most of the flux is unknown, so further maturation would be useful.
uncertainties: Individual attribution in a very large collaboration.
The origin of the diffuse flux is not resolved.
Earlier pioneers (DUMAND, Baikal, AMANDA) are outside the supplied credit.
